messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@mediapulse.com>

Subject: Mediapulse onboarding — acceptance targets + proposed runbook

Hi team / Samir,

Quick handoff: Mediapulse (Samir) is ready for the performance acceptance run next week. I attached a concise load_plan (mediapulse_load_plan.yaml) — please review. Key acceptance targets the customer agreed to: 
- Target p95 token latency: <= 200 ms (steady-state)
- Tail (99.9th) should be under 500 ms for sequences <= 256 tokens
- Sustained throughput target: 500 qps (inference requests) for their 1-model traffic mix
- Cold-start ramp tolerance: 5% error budget during warmup window (first 10 minutes)

Proposed schedule (UTC-7):
- Warmup and smoke: Mon 2026-11-01 08:00–08:30 PT
- Full load run: Mon 2026-11-01 09:00–11:00 PT
- Results summary and sync: Mon 2026-11-01 14:00 PT (30 min)

Open asks for Mediapulse:
- Provide a test API key or allow our test client IPs (list in the yaml)
- Confirm representative request distribution (attachments include a simplified traffic mix)
- Share a contact for their infra team in case we need to open ports/whitelist during the run

I recommend Karthik take the runbook lead, Monica to own telemetry checks, and Laura to coordinate the customer-facing readout. Samir — are the times above workable?

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mediapulse_load_plan.yaml (YAML run config, IP whitelist section included)

Thanks Samir — confirming schedule + a few technical notes for the run: 

Runbook highlights (short):
- Environment: Dedicated shard on rtx-a100-80gb (reserved capacity) with pinned model version v3.2.
- Batching: we'll run with adaptive batching disabled for the primary pass so we can measure per-request latency; second pass will enable batching to show potential cost curves.
- KV cache: warm-up phase will pre-populate prefix cache for top 500 prompts (Ben's yaml includes seed set).
- Metrics we will collect: p50/p95/p99 latencies (per-token and end-to-end), qps, gpu utilization, request error rate, tail-latency distribution, and memory pressure.
- Failure modes: any sustained error rate >1% for 5m triggers an automatic stop and rollback to a lower concurrency profile.

About the warmup: a 20-minute ramp is fine — we'll treat the first 20 minutes as warmup window (not counted against acceptance), then run three 20-minute steady-state sweeps at target QPS (500) with 5-minute cool-downs between.

Credentials: please provide the test API key and confirm the sandbox ACL for the following Redwood test IPs: 35.201.?.? (full list in drive link). If whitelisting isn't possible, we can run from a VPN peer or ask for short-term credentials.

I'll attach a small results template (CSV header) we'll populate live. After the run I'll share the raw CSV and a 1-page acceptance note.

Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-run: quick summary + artifacts (initial pass)

Samir / team — thanks for running with us this morning. TL;DR: primary acceptance targets met with one tail spike during sweep #2. Attachments: mediapulse_results_20261030.csv and tail_latency_screenshot_20261030.png. Full Drive artifacts uploaded to the shared folder.

Key observations:
- p95 steady-state: 185 ms (target <= 200 ms)
- p99 steady-state: 360 ms (within tolerance)
- tail 99.9th: 720 ms during a 90s window in sweep #2 when an upstream cache miss coincided with a brief retry burst — we observed increased GPU queueing for ~12s.
- Sustained throughput: 510 qps average across three sweeps.
- Error rate: 0.4% overall (requests that timed out were retried by the client and succeeded).

Immediate remediation steps we propose (if you want to tighten tail):
1) Increase prefix cache prefill to top 2k prompts (reduces cache miss blast radius)
2) Add a short, client-side jitter to retry backoff to avoid synchronized retry storms
3) Second-pass with batching enabled to measure cost/latency tradeoffs (we saw ~12% token-cost reduction with batching in local sim)

Next steps / asks:
- Samir: confirm whether Mediapulse considers the current tail acceptable for go/no-go (happy to run a follow-up sweep with the cache change).
- Olivia: can you confirm the sandbox key rotation window? We will need the key active for 48 hours while we upload artifacts and run a second pass if requested.

Thanks again — I'll post the raw CSV and screenshots to Drive and schedule the 30-min readout for Mon 2026-11-01 14:00 PT unless you request another time.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mediapulse_results_20261030.csv, tail_latency_screenshot_20261030.png
